causalPreservation migrated. SHA 02840a9 on m1/resolution. Gate: align 178, fixtures 110, interview 81, laws 81, recall 41, scalafmtCheckAll clean, run as the last action before commit.

HOW MUCH THE NUMBER MOVES: it does not. It was None on the worked example and it stays None. I am reporting that plainly because the bead asks for the movement and "none" is the honest answer here - but the change is not therefore cosmetic, and the reason is worth more than the number would have been.

WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGED: the abstention can now say why it abstained. The participant reached 0 of the source's 3 causal edges. Before, that was a bare None - indistinguishable from a source that HAS no causal structure to preserve. Those are different objects now: conditioning 0 of 3, versus 0 of 0. Only the first is a fact about the participant; the second is a fact about the stimulus. An abstention that cannot say which one it is is barely better than the 1.0 it replaced, because a reader still cannot act on it.

That distinction is pinned by assertion, not left to the docstring - both abstain, and their totalMass must differ.

WHY A COUNT AND NOT A MASS, since this looks like it contradicts the specificity ruling I applied an hour ago: localizability is defined ON source mass and describes how concentrated that mass is, so summing mass was the only coherent denominator there. A causal edge is a discrete object in the source graph - recalled or not - and there is no partial edge for a mass to measure. Applying "always sum the mass" here would have been cargo-culting the ruling instead of applying it. If you disagree, this is the one to push back on.

MUTATION KILLED: collapsing the support denominator to the conditioning set, which makes support identically 1.0 - the classic way to make a coverage figure look complete. totalMass reads 0.0 against the required 3.0.

FILED, NOT SILENTLY CHANGED - and this one needs you. The conditioning test is `visitation.getOrElse(a, 0.0) > 0.5`, a hard threshold: a node visited with 0.51 mass counts in full, one with 0.49 counts not at all. That cliff decides which edges enter the denominator, so touching it moves published numbers, which makes it yours and not mine. It is the same 0.5-cliff family you catalogued in the interview module. I have left it exactly as it was and said so in the commit body so a future reader does not think the migration blessed it.

Seven of the fifteen fields are now migrated. Remaining: uniformCoverage, discourseChronology, worldChronology, the six external mass terms, distortedMass and its facet map, and perUnitLocalizability. Continuing unless you want the pending queue drained first - it is now c1049f2, e538a09, 2adfff2, aee72ed, 4383a85, 02840a9.
